title: Consolidate host IO surface and streamline thread handoff to cut prefill/decode overhead
creator: Ravi Menon
description: Problem: Host-side cost for prefill->decode pipeline is dominated by repeated small memcpy operations, lock contention in the generic threadpool, and a chatty IO surface between scheduler and GPU bridge. This ticket consolidates the IO surface, introduces a small serialized staging path for tiny prefills, and replaces a handful of mutex-heavy handoffs with lock-free rendezvous that preserve priority ordering. Goal is to reduce median prefill latency by 15-25% and 95th percentile CPU utilization for inference hosts by 20% on typical chat workloads. Deliverables: consolidated C API for host->gpu staging, lightweight per-request handoff token, thread affinity hints for the GPU bridge, and integration tests showing end-to-end perf improvements.
acceptance_criteria: New host IO surface (hostbridge_v2) implemented and behind feature flag
Median prefill latency reduced by >=15% on internal chat benchmark (seq_len=128, batch=1-8)
95th percentile host CPU utilization during steady-state inference reduced by >=20%
End-to-end correctness tests for prefills and KV cache preserved (no regressed outputs)
Design doc and API compatibility notes published in Confluence
Feature gated rollout plan and telemetry to detect regressions in production
comments: 2026-02-12 — Spike complete: measured 1.8x increase in memcpy syscalls for micro-prefills (<=512 bytes). Confirmed lock contention hotspots in threadpool_worker::pop(). Recorded flamegraph and heap profile (links in attachments). — Ravi

2026-02-18 — Design review: decided to add a compact staging slab allocator that coalesces small writes and exposes a single ring buffer per-GPU rather than per-request buffers. Preference for lock-free single-producer single-consumer queue for the hot path. Trade-off: slightly more complex edge-case handling for torn writes. — Feedback from Lina (infra lead): prefer explicit backpressure path for bursty workloads.

2026-02-22 — Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4210. Early perf: median prefill latency -12%, p95 CPU -9%. Observed occasional latency spikes when slab recycling falls behind. — Marta

2026-02-28 — Implemented thread-affinity hints and lightweight handoff token. Reduced mutex hold times in threadpool by moving queue metadata to per-worker cacheline-aligned structures. Unit tests updated. — Marta

2026-03-05 — Integration run against canary cluster: 48h soak showed steady improvements but one regression case where very large batched prefills (batch>=64) saw negligible improvement. Added adaptive bypass for large batches to use previous path. — Ravi
2026-03-10 — Code review notes from Eng SRE: ensure ABI stability for private deployments; add feature flag env var and metric for slab_recycles. Added smoke tests to nightly. — Lina
2026-03-12 — Ready for performance signoff. Plan: enable behind runtime-prefill-consolidation feature flag for 10% of host fleet next week, monitor prefill_latency_p50/p95 and host_cpu_user. — Marta
